title: In 135 IBL mouse sessions, regions with more CA1 and subiculum axon input had more spikes at CA1 population bursts; with strict immobility, this link was not clear beyond brain division
abstract: Question: do the axon outputs of the hippocampal formation tell which mouse brain regions increase or decrease spiking at hippocampal ripple-like events? Data: IBL Brain-Wide Map 2026 Q2, 136 sessions with a CA1 probe; spike windows of all probes (last 600 s of the task and the passive spontaneous period); Knox 2019 connectome model (CA1 + subiculum output). Method: CA1 population bursts from multi-unit spikes in the most bursty 200-um CA1 depth window (z >= 3, immobile, away from task events); unit modulation index (MI) -50..+50 ms vs -2.0..-0.5 s; region means; partial Spearman with control for distance to CA1, brain division and rate; 1,000 spatial surrogate maps; plan hashed before data were read. Results: 19,588 good units in 83 regions (135 sessions). Lateral septum, septofimbrial nucleus, retrosplenial cortex, accumbens and hippocampus increased; sensory thalamus (VPM, PO, PF) and medulla decreased; maps agreed between task and spontaneous periods (rho 0.70). Planned H1 was supported: partial rho 0.30 (spatial p 0.013; 95th percentile of 291 sources). Thalamus decreased (median MI -0.035, p 0.026); isocortex did not clearly increase. LF-band check in 6 probes: 150-250 Hz power rose at events (AUC 0.54-0.94); in 3 probes 28-55% of events had z >= 2. Post hoc: random immobile times also gave MI values that followed wiring (rho 0.42) because the baseline could include wheel movement. With fully immobile windows and a random-time contrast (33,898 events) this artefact disappeared; wiring still correlated with modulation (rho 0.43) and predicted it beyond distance (partial 0.37, p 0.004), but not clearly beyond brain division (partial 0.15, p 0.13, 95% CI -0.15 to 0.35). Limitations: spike-based ripple proxy validated in 6 probes only; region-level confound of division and hippocampal output; smoothed model connectome; head-fixed task mice.

display.caption: A: mean modulation index (MI, -50..+50 ms vs -2.0..-0.5 s) at CA1 population bursts for 83 mouse brain regions (IBL Brain-Wide Map, 135 sessions), ordered by division. Bars: planned MI (blue > 0, orange < 0). Black dots: post hoc strict-immobility contrast MI(event) - MI(random immobile times). B-D: population rate around the event peak, normalised to -500..-300 ms, by division (n = units).

A: planned test H1, rank residuals of Knox 2019 CA1+SUB output and region MI after control for distance to CA1, division and rate (partial rho 0.30, spatial p 0.013). B: the same with the strict state-matched MI (0.15, p 0.13). C: H1 statistic in all analyses; tick = 95th percentile of 1,000 spatial surrogates; blue = p < 0.05. D: task vs spontaneous region maps. E: partial rho of each of 291 single Knox sources. F: session-bootstrap 95% intervals of raw and partial rho.

A: CA1 150-250 Hz LFP envelope (z) around spike-detected events in 6 probes, on detection-layer channels (blue) and all CA1 channels (grey). B: events per session in the last 600 s of the task and in the passive spontaneous period (dashed line: 30-event minimum). C: event rates in the two conditions.
